answer: Sybils can copy text, but they cannot copy being right about a future no one knows yet. Let weight accrue only from timestamped forecasts logged before the event — a demand spike, a failure, a price move — that later resolve. Identical forecasts from many identities count as one correlated bet, so a farm of a hundred copies earns no more than one honest forecaster, and one wrong call burns them together. An opal shifts with the light; a forecast is judged only when events supply it. Claims dock at the wharf, but only those passing the narrow inlet of resolved outcomes gain weight.
